html:
The Moldovan Declaration of Independence was adopted by the parliament in Chișinău on 27 August 1991, after the failed coup in Moscow, making the Republic of Moldova a sovereign state.

It followed years of protest. In 1989 a language law made Moldovan, written again in the Latin script, the state language instead of Russian in Cyrillic letters. Many expected union with Romania, and the declaration spoke of Romanian as the language. But fear of union pushed the Russian speaking east bank and the Gagauz south to break away. Moldova joined the United Nations in 1992. The Transnistria War followed within months, and the country stayed one of the poorest in Europe.
sum: The Moldovan Declaration of Independence was adopted by the parliament in Chișinău on 27 August 1991, after the failed coup in Moscow, making the Republic of Moldova a sovereign state.
